prompt:
Design a responsive admin page layout that includes a sticky header at the top of the page. The header should be white in light mode and change to dark in dark mode. The header should also contain a navbar. 

Within the navbar, start by placing a small logo image on the left for small screens, and at the center for large screens. On the right, include a search bar that appears on large screens. The search bar should contain a search icon as well as a text input field with a placeholder "Search". 

Also, create two square buttons with no explicit borders, however, when hovered over, they should change background color. Each button should contain an image. 

Next to the buttons, include a dropdown, activated by a button with a user's profile picture. In the dropdown, include sections for "Signed in as" with user's email, and another section with a number of links each accompanied by an image. The links should represent "Newsletter", "Purchases", "Downloads", and "Team Account". 

Remember that the header should adapt responsively to different screen sizes.
short_prompt: Create a responsive admin page with a sticky header that changes color based on light or dark mode. Include a navbar with a logo, search bar (for large screens), two image-contained buttons, and a user profile dropdown with specified links. The design should be adaptive to different screen sizes.

prompt:
Create an Application Statistics Dashboard section that displays various metrics. This section should be divided into four parts, each part for a different metric. 

The metrics to be displayed are as follows:

1) Total Users: This part should have an image placeholder followed by a description with a tooltip that explains what "Total Users" means. It should then display the total number of users and the percentage increase or decrease with an accompanying placeholder image. 

2) Sessions: This part should have an image placeholder and the "Sessions" label. It should then display the percentage value and the percentage increase or decrease with an accompanying placeholder image.

3) Average Click Rate: This part should have an image placeholder followed by a description with a tooltip that explains what "Average Click Rate" means. It should then display the average click rate and a statement "Need attention" with an accompanying placeholder image. 

4) Pageviews: This part should have an image placeholder followed by the "Pageviews" label. It should then display the total pageviews and "2 warnings" with an accompanying placeholder image.

The section should have a dark mode. For dark mode, component colors should be switched to darker tones. Each part should have dividers separating them, and their content should be aligned in rows with space between columns. Placeholders for images should be filled with actual images later. 

The dashboard section should be centered and have appropriate padding. The section should also be responsive, with the items expanding into separate rows and columns on smaller screens.
short_prompt: Design an Application Statistics Dashboard with four sections: Total Users, Sessions, Average Click Rate, and Pageviews. Each section needs an image placeholder, relevant data displays, and tooltips where specified. Implement dark mode and design elements like spacing and dividers. Ensure it's centered, padded, responsive for various screen sizes and image placeholders are replaceable with actual images.

Create an application status component that shows project statistics, displayed in center-aligned cards. The overall component should be a grid of three cards, each card for a category ("Projects", "Successful Conversions", "Failed Conversions"). 

Each card should be a white background box separated by gaps and contoured by a border with gentle shadow for a 3D effect. Also, they should have rounded corners for a softer appearance. 

Inside each card, place three sections; the first being a title consisting of a filled circle symbol next to uppercase text and the second being a numeric value showing the statistic in large, bold font. It should contain a title, numeric value in bold font, and a line indicating the percentage change with an icon and last week's stat. The colors should indicate improvement, decline or static value. Ensure it is dark mode compatible.

prompt:
Create an application form layout with the following features:

1. The form should be contained within a card-like background pattern for segregation from the rest of the body content.
2. There should be a section for the applicant to submit their full name, email, phone, and current company.
3. The next section should be for uploading a resume/CV and a place to write a personal summary.
4. A section should also be there for providing social media and personal website URLs.
5. Finally, there should be an area where they can state their desired salary and possible start date.
6. Before the submit button, there should be a checkbox that allows the users to permit the site to process their personal information.

The form should collect applicants' personal details, allow for resume upload, a personal summary, and social media/website URLs. It should include a field for desired salary, start date, and a checkbox for consent to process personal information. The form should have a full-width blue submit button.

name: Af submit app
prompt:
Create a responsive layout for an application submission form. The form should be placed centrally and contain the following elements:

1. An abstract background image at the top, under which a button with "Upload header" text and an image icon should be placed.
2. A logo upload section with an image placeholder thumbnail and two buttons - one labeled "Upload Logo" with an image icon and another red colored labeled "Delete".
3. A series of labeled input fields placed vertically and spaced evenly for the user to enter their project name, project URL.
4. A block for users to upload their project preview image, with the option to either browse their device or drag and drop a file. It should also have a note indicating the maximum file size for the upload.
5. A dropdown selection field for users to select the category of their project.
6. A text area for users to provide a detailed description of their project.
7. At the bottom of the form, there should be a blue button labeled "Submit your project".
   
Ensure that the form is contained within a rounded rectangular section that has a white background. All input fields and buttons should also be rounded and have variations upon interacting (like hover, focus, or being disabled). Don't forget to make the form compatible with a dark mode.
short_prompt: Design a responsive, centrally placed application form with a background image, logo upload section, input fields for project details, dropdown for category, text area for project description, and a submit button. The design should be interactive and compatible with dark mode.

prompt:
Create an application invoice that is initially hidden but is revealed when a button titled "Open offcanvas" is clicked. This invoice should be designed to slide from the right part of the screen (an offcanvas element). 

The first part of the offcanvas element should have a text button "Close" which when clicked hides the offcanvas element. There should be a place for an image placeholder and this part should be set against an abstract background.

The next part should be a round image placeholder set against a white circle. This should be followed by the invoice title and number, centered in the middle.

The following section should include three key invoice details: the amount paid, the date of the payment and the payment method. Each of these should have a descriptive text followed by the actual data. The payment method should include another image placeholder alongside the method details.

Next, include a summary section with an uppercased title "Summary". This section should contain an unordered list of items showing what the payment is for and the amount.

Finally, provide two options at the bottom right of the offcanvas: one to download the invoice as a PDF and the other to print it. Each option should include an image placeholder and text describing the action. Also, include customer service contact details at the very bottom of the offcanvas for any queries the user may have.
short_prompt: Develop a hidden application invoice that appears by clicking "Open offcanvas". This offcanvas will slide from the right with a "Close" button, image placeholder, and invoice details. It needs a summary section and options for downloading and printing the invoice. Also, include customer service contact details at the bottom.

name: Ai modal
prompt: Create a 'Open modal' button that is horizontally and vertically centered on the page. The button should have padding to its content, text should be small, font should be bold, and corners should be slightly rounded. The background color of the button should be a shade of blue and text color should be white. On hovering over the button, the background color should slightly darken. Also, if the button is disabled, reduce its opacity to make it look disabled and prevent any cursor events on it.
short_prompt: Design a 'Open modal' button, centered on the page, with padding, small bold text, lightly rounded corners, and a blue background. On hover, the background darkens, and if disabled, the button is transparent and doesn't react to cursor events.

name: Ai welcome page
prompt:
Create an AI welcome page named "Application ai prompt". The page should be a vertical layout, taking up the full height of the screen. It should contain two main sections.

In the first section, place a centered image placeholder at the top, followed by a large, bold title saying "Welcome to Preline AI". Beneath the title, insert a paragraph with a lighter color text that reads "Your AI-powered copilot for the web".

Beneath the first section, add a smaller-scale section that includes an input text box with the placeholder text "Ask me anything...". To the right of the text box, include two small round buttons each containing a placeholder image. The first button should be transparent, while the second button should have a light gray background.

At the very bottom of the page, add a centered footer with copyright information stating "© 2024 Preline. A product of Htmlstream". Make the "Htmlstream" text a hyperlink to "http://htmlstream.com/" in new browsing context and style it to underline when hovered over.
short_prompt: Design a full-screen, vertically laid AI welcome page with two sections: an image placeholder, a bold title "Welcome to Preline AI", and a paragraph "Your AI-powered copilot for the web" in the first section. A smaller second section should have a text box reading "Ask me anything...", two round image buttons with different backgrounds. Add a footer at the bottom with copyright info, a "Htmlstream" hyperlink opening in a new tab, and a hover underline effect.

name: Ai with sidebar
prompt: Create an HTML component named "Application ai prompt". It should fall under the category of "Ai with a sidebar". The main component should be a div with a fixed position, a list for navigation, some images as links in the navigation list, and some have hover effects. Add placeholders for 5 list items in the navigation section, with "New chat", "Preline AI Discord", "Save conversation", "Updates & FAQ", and "Upgrade Plan" as placeholders for the text associated with each link respectively. The "Upgrade Plan" should have a gradient color effect. At the bottom of the sidebar add a status indicator showing "Active 12,320 people" and a "Sign in" button.
short_prompt: Create an HTML "Application ai prompt" component under "Ai with a sidebar" category. It should include a fixed-position div with a navigation list containing images as links, hover effects, placeholders for 5 items: "New chat", "Preline AI Discord", "Save conversation", "Updates & FAQ", "Upgrade Plan" (with a gradient color). Add a "Sign in" button and a status indicator displaying "Active 12,320 people" at the sidebar's bottom.

name: Header center aligned in lime
prompt:
Create a navigation bar for a website header. The navbar should be centered and styled in a lime color scheme. The navbar should contain the organization's logo on the leftmost side. Next to the logo, there should be five navigational links: "Work," "Services," "About," "Careers," "Blog."

On the rightmost side of the navbar, there should be two buttons. The first one is a "Sign in" button with a border and a hover effect that changes the background to a lighter gray. The second button is a "Hire us" button styled with a lime-colored background and a hover effect that darkens the lime color.

Finally, there should be a mobile menu button that is only visible on smaller (mobile) screens. The menu should animate when clicked, revealing the same links as in the desktop view. This button should have a simple design with an image placeholder. Make sure to include focus, transition, and disabled states for all buttons and links for improved user accessibility.

Also, ensure all elements are properly aligned and positioned for various screen sizes, from mobile to desktop.
short_prompt: Design a centered, lime-colored website navbar with the organization's logo and five links ("Work," "Services," "About," "Careers," "Blog"). On the right, include "Sign in" and "Hire us" buttons with specific hover effects, and a mobile menu button for smaller screens with all the links. Make sure all elements work for various screen sizes and have focus, transition, and disabled states.

name: Header primary background
prompt: Design a navigations navbar for the header with a primary background. It should have a maximum width of 85rem and it should be centered with auto margins. There should be a padding of 10 units on the top and bottom, and 4 units on the left and right. On small screens, the horizontal padding should be 6 units and on large screens, it should be 8 units.
short_prompt: Create a centered navigation bar with a primary background, max width of 85rem and padding of 10 units top-bottom, and 4 units left-right. Adjust the horizontal padding to 6 units on small screens and 8 on large screens.

name: Mega menu dropdown style with icon and description
prompt:
Design a large or 'mega' dropdown style navigation menu with the addition of icons and descriptions for each menu item. The maximum width of the menu should be 85rem and it should be centered on the page.
Also, add a padding of 10 units to the top and bottom, 4 units on the sides for small screens, 6 units for medium screens, and 8 units for large screens.
short_prompt: Create a mega dropdown navigation menu with icons and descriptions for each item, centered on the page and max width of 85rem. Add padding: 10 units top and bottom, 4 units on the sides for small screens, 6 for medium screens, and 8 for large screens.

name: Mega menu custom size with icon text link and background gray card
prompt: Create a large custom-sized navigation menu component. This menu should have icon text links and a background featuring a gray card design. The component should be centered with automatic margins on the x-axis, and it should have padding on the y-axis. The maximum width should be 85rem with horizontal padding increasing responsively for small, large, and extra-large screens.
short_prompt: Design a custom navigation menu with text icon links and a gray card background, centered with auto margins on x-axis and y-axis padding. Its maximum width should be 85rem with responsive horizontal padding for varying screen sizes.

name: Mega menu header
prompt: Create a header component for a mega menu navigation system. The component should be of a fixed maximum width. The component should be centered with auto margins on the side. Add padding on the top and bottom, with additional padding along the sides. Make sure that the side padding is responsive, and increases on small, large and extra large screens respectively.
short_prompt: Design a header for a mega menu with a fixed maximum width, centered with auto margins, and with padding on all sides that adjusts responsively on different screen sizes.

name: Boxed layout
prompt:
Create a basic layout component named "Layouts basic" under the category "Boxed layout". The layout should have a maximum width of 85 rem and should be horizontally centered. It should occupy a minimum height equivalent to the full screen.

The layout should have a white background and borders on both sides colored gray-200. A padding of 10 on the y-axis and 4 on the x-axis should be applied to the layout. Make the left and right padding of the layout to 6 for small devices, and 8 for large devices.

When the layout is viewed in dark mode, change the background to neutral-800 and the side borders color to gray-700.
short_prompt: Design a "Layouts basic" component under "Boxed layout", with an 85 rem max width, full-screen minimum height, centrally aligned horizontally. It should have a white background, gray-200 side borders, a y-axis padding of 10, and an x-axis padding of 4 that adjusts to 6 (small devices) or 8 (large devices). In dark mode, change the background to neutral-800 and the border color to gray-700.

Create a basic layout for a cover page. The layout should be centered and have a maximum width of 50rem. It should consist of a header, main section, and footer.

prompt:
Create a cookie banner that needs to be scrollable and should have collapse-able sections. It should be a fixed and centered window with rounded corners and a drop shadow. The banner should have a heading asking for permission to use cookies and a brief summary of why cookies are used, followed by a section explaining in detail with image indicators what cookies do and how they're used. This section should be divided into three parts, each part containing an image and a small paragraph of text.

After this, there should be another paragraph explaining the use of external tools for analytics followed by a paragraph explaining how the user can control their cookie preferences with a link to the cookie policy. 

Next, there should be two collapsible sections titled "Essential cookies" and "Optional cookies". Each section should be visible when clicked on. The "Essential cookies" section should explain why these cookies are required. The "Optional cookies" section should explain what these cookies are for and it should have a link for more information.

The banner should end with two call-to-action buttons, one allowing only essential cookies, and the other allowing all cookies. These buttons should be side by side and provide a visual feedback when hovered. The entire banner should follow a light and dark theme respectively as per user preference.
short_prompt: Design a scrollable, fixed, centered cookie banner with rounded corners, a drop shadow, and collapsible sections. It needs a header, explanations about cookies and external tools, a section to control cookie preferences, two parts about essential and optional cookies, and two call-to-action buttons. The design should adhere to light and dark themes.

name: Cookies simple with icon and dismiss button
prompt:
Design a cookie banner component that is placed at the bottom right of the page. This banner should be a box with a white(or dark) background and rounded edges with a subtle shadow. Inside this banner, on a single horizontal line, place an image placeholder, a small paragraph of text, and a button.

The paragraph of text should inform the user about the cookies policy, the link to the cookies policy should be a different color and underlined when hovered. Next to the text, put a dismiss button. This button should only contain an image placeholder and be round with text that only screen readers can see. When hovered, make the button change its background color. When disabled, reduce the button opacity and disable any events.
short_prompt: Create a cookie banner with an image, descriptive text, and a dismiss button; placed bottom-right with a shaded white/dark background, rounded edges. prompt:
Create a fixed, full-width web banner that appears at the bottom of the page. This banner will be presenting information about the use of cookies on the website. This information should be contained within a heading titled "We use cookies" followed by a paragraph explaining why cookies are used. 

In addition to that, provide four options for users to select from: "Necessary", "Preferences", "Statistics", and "Marketing". Each of these options should be represented with its own label and a checkbox.

Next, create three buttons: one that gives approval for all the cookie types ("Allow all"), another that gives approval for the selected types ("Allow selection"), and a third one that dismisses all of them ("Reject all").

Lastly, make sure to include a placeholder for the company's logo on the left side. The design should be modern, with a clear and clean layout that neatly organizes all the text and options.
short_prompt: Design a full-width cookie banner at the page's bottom, with a header "We use cookies" and an explanation paragraph, four labeled checkboxes for "Necessary", "Preferences", "Statistics", and "Marketing", and three buttons, "Allow all", "Allow selection", and "Reject all". Include a company logo placeholder on the left, in a modern, organized, and clean layout.

name: Cookies fullwidth centered content
html:
Cookie Settings

We use cookies to improve your experience and for marketing. Visit our Cookies Policy to learn more.
prompt:
Generate a HTML component for a cookie banner. The banner should be positioned at the bottom of the page, stretched full-width, and above other elements on the page. It should have a light background with a subtle shadow and a border.

The banner should contain a title "Cookie Settings" and a descriptive text that explains the use of cookies, with a link leading to a "Cookies Policy" in this text. 

There should also be two buttons for user to either "Agree" or "Reject". 

The "Agree" button should be filled with a strong color and have white text. On hover, make the color slightly darker. The "Reject" button should have a lighter color with darker text. On hover, make the background color slightly darker. For accessibility purposes, ensure that the buttons have a visual change (opacity) when they are disabled.

Make sure the banner adapts well to dark mode, changing the background, border, text, and link colors appropriately. Make the content centered and fully responsive.
short_prompt: Create a responsive HTML cookie banner at the page bottom, above other components, with a light background, shadow, border, and changeable dark mode colors. It must contain a title "Cookie Settings", explanatory text with a "Cookies Policy" link, and two buttons - "Agree" (strong-colored, white-text, darker on hover) and "Reject" (light-colored, dark-text, darker on hover). Buttons should change opacity when disabled.

prompt:

Ensure the banner maintains good visibility on both light and dark mode.

Company News

January 18, 2023

At preline, our mission has always been focused on bringing openness and transparency to the design process. We've always believed that by providing a space where designers can share ongoing work not only empowers them to make better products, it also helps them grow.

We're proud to be a part of creating a more open culture and to continue building a product that supports this vision.

Working process

As we've grown, we've seen how Preline has helped companies such as Spotify, Microsoft, Airbnb, Facebook, and Intercom bring their designers closer together to create amazing things. We've also learned that when the culture of sharing is brought in earlier, the better teams adapt and communicate with one another.

That's why we are excited to share that we now have a free version of Preline, which will allow individual designers, startups and other small teams a chance to create a culture of openness early on.

To say that switching to Preline has been life-changing is an understatement. My business has tripled and I got my life back.

Nicole Grazioso

Bringing the culture of sharing to everyone

We know the power of sharing is real, and we want to create an opportunity for everyone to try Preline and explore how transformative open communication can be. Now you can have a team of one or two designers and unlimited spectators (think PMs, management, marketing, etc.) share work and explore the design process earlier.
